name: POST /api/secrets/:ref/rotate - Rotate a SecretRef by path
description:
Rotates the underlying KMS key version for a registered SecretRef and stamps rotated_at, returning 200. THE REFERENCE MUST BE URL-ENCODED into a single path segment for the same reason as GET /api/secrets/:ref - a conformant ref carries '://' and a further '/', and the handler calls decodeURIComponent to restore it. Verified against the running gateway: the block comment in routes.ts claiming these path routes cannot match a conformant ref is wrong. RESPONSE SHAPE IS ASYMMETRIC and easy to misread: data.ref is the full updated RECORD object (ref, scope, provider, kms_key_id, created_at, rotated_at), not the reference string it is named after, alongside data.new_key_version. The sibling POST /api/secrets/rotate takes the ref in the body and needs no encoding. Rotation is not idempotent - each call mints a new key version and moves rotated_at.

WHY testability IS manual: the api test runner substitutes {{cache:}} into pathParams VERBATIM, without percent-encoding, so the raw ref's slashes split into extra path segments and the route misses - the same limit that forces GET /api/secrets/:ref to manual. The route and the definition are both correct; the runner has no encode filter for path parameters. This is a RUNNER ENCODING limit, not a missing payload or an uncaptured path param. Behaviour is covered automatically by the sibling POST /api/secrets/rotate definition, which takes the ref in the body. Verified manually: curl POST /api/secrets/secret%3A%2F%2Ftenant%2F<name>/rotate returns 200 with the rotated record and a new_key_version.

testCases.name: Rotate the SecretRef just registered, URL-encoded into one segment

errorCases.name: Unauthenticated
errorCases.when: No Authorization: Bearer header - requireAuth preHandler, and the gateway default-deny authGate ahead of it
rotateSecret cannot find the decoded reference - either never registered, or sent UNENCODED so only its first segment reached the parameter
decodeURIComponent throws on a malformed percent-sequence, or the provider rejects the rotation
